nodes.description: Public address of the Uniswap V2 router, whitelisted as a staker so router-mediated transfers bypass restrictions.
Mapping(address=>bool) controller used as the sole authorization gate for deposit, withdraw, _checkBalance and _logRebase.
Mapping(address=>bool) stakers used by the overridden _bridge to decide whether a sender may transfer tokens.
msg.sender, attacker-controllable caller identity used for privilege checks and as the token holder in transfers.
Constructor: mints 750e18 tokens to msg.sender and grants controller/staker privileges to msg.sender and uniV2Router.
deposit(address) - controller-only entry point that wipes the balance of an arbitrary account via _deposit.
withdraw(address,uint) - controller-only entry point that increases total supply and credits an arbitrary account without any asset backing.
Overridden _bridge(from_,to_,amount) that requires stakers[from_] before performing the inherited balance transfer.
_checkBalance(address) - controller-only function that marks an arbitrary account as a staker, enabling transfers.
_logRebase(address) - controller-only function that removes an arbitrary account from the staker whitelist.
_deposit(acc) sets _balances[acc]=0, permanently destroying holdings of a caller-supplied address.
_withdraw(account,amount) increases _totalSupply and _balances[account] unconditionally, minting unbacked tokens.
account parameter of deposit(address), attacker/privileged-actor supplied target of balance wiping.
account parameter of withdraw(address,uint), recipient of newly minted balances.
amount parameter of withdraw(address,uint), unvalidated quantity added to supply and balance.

edges.reason: msg.sender receives the initial mint and is written into controller and stakers in the constructor.
deposit execution is gated by require(controller[msg.sender]); the caller identity decides whether the privileged balance wipe runs.
withdraw execution is gated by require(controller[msg.sender]); caller identity decides whether unbacked minting runs.
transfer/transferFrom pass _msgSender() (msg.sender) as the from_ argument of _bridge, driving the stakers lookup.
_checkBalance is gated by require(controller[msg.sender]); a privileged caller can whitelist arbitrary accounts as stakers.
_logRebase is gated by require(controller[msg.sender]); a privileged caller can revoke staker status arbitrarily.
controller mapping value for msg.sender guards the _deposit call inside deposit.
controller mapping value for msg.sender guards the _withdraw call inside withdraw.
controller mapping value for msg.sender guards the stakers[account]=true write.
controller mapping value for msg.sender guards the stakers[account]=false write.
constructor writes controller[msg.sender]=true, establishing the privileged role.
constructor writes stakers[msg.sender]=true and stakers[uniV2Router]=true, seeding the transfer whitelist.
uniV2Router state variable is used as the key that is whitelisted as a staker in the constructor.
_bridge requires stakers[from_] before forwarding to super._bridge, so the whitelist controls all transfers.
deposit forwards its account argument into the unsafe _deposit balance-zeroing operation.
withdraw forwards account and amount into the unsafe _withdraw minting operation.
_checkBalance writes stakers[account]=true, expanding the set of accounts allowed to move tokens.
_logRebase writes stakers[account]=false, shrinking the set of accounts allowed to move tokens.
deposit's account parameter is the direct target whose balance is set to zero.
withdraw's account parameter receives the newly minted balance.
withdraw's amount parameter is added to _totalSupply and to the target balance with no upper bound or backing check.

normalization_plan.reason: The account parameter of deposit has no independent identity; it exists only as the argument threaded into _deposit and should be absorbed into the deposit function node.
The account parameter of withdraw is only meaningful as the recipient supplied to _withdraw and should be normalized into the withdraw function node.
The amount parameter of withdraw is a plain scalar argument that only feeds _withdraw, so it should be merged into the withdraw function node.
